baseline_facts.content: Cough started approximately five days ago.
Constant nasal discharge for five days.
Sometimes feels chilly and needs a blanket.
Has not checked temperature with a thermometer.
Drinking well and holding down fluids.
No history of recurrent chest infections.
Last blood pressure check was a while ago.
Patient cannot recall blood pressure stability.
A blood test about three weeks ago was normal.
Lives with a partner and a dog.
Does not check blood glucose at home.
Takes Lemsip two to three times per day.
Doctor advised purchasing a thermometer to check temperature.
Doctor advised to seek care if temperature remains above 37.5 or 38.
Doctor advised to seek care if cough worsens.
Doctor advised to seek care if cough produces lots of phlegm.
Doctor advised to seek care if coughing up blood.
Doctor advised to seek care if blood comes from the nose.
Doctor advised to seek care if shortness of breath develops.
Doctor advised to seek care if chest pain develops.
Doctor noted diabetes increases risk of bacterial infection.
Doctor discussed potential antibiotics if symptoms do not settle.
Doctor advised not to take other paracetamol-containing products with Lemsip.
Doctor advised against daytime use of cough syrup.
Doctor allowed a small amount of cough syrup at night if unable to sleep.
Doctor advised maintaining regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups.

candidate_facts.content: Diarrhea occurred at the onset of symptoms.

Patient was advised to seek consultation if cough worsens.
Patient was advised to seek consultation if signs of bacterial infection appear.
Potential antibiotic consideration if symptoms worsen.
Patient was advised to continue using Lemsip.
Patient was advised to avoid additional paracetamol-containing products.
Patient was advised to use cough syrup at night if necessary.
Patient was advised to have regular diabetes check-ups with GP.
Patient was advised to have regular blood pressure monitoring as per GP advice.
